reason: E1 shows MA+SPS can produce a HEA with good density and hardness, but it uses a different alloy system (NiCoCr-based) and does not involve oxide dispersoids, so it only weakly supports the feasibility of the processing route. E3 demonstrates MA+SPS for a refractory HEA (CrMoNbWV) but again without Y2O3, providing no evidence for dispersion, stability, or mechanical effects of oxide nanoparticles. The key premises about Y2O3 dispersion, its stability, strengthening mechanism, and preservation of ductility are entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS) can produce refractory HEAs with fine microstructures
Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a refractory HEA matrix via MA with dispersion control
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles remain stable during SPS consolidation at 950–1150 °C
Y2O3 dispersoids significantly enhance high-temperature strength and creep resistance via dislocation pinning
Low volume fraction of Y2O3 preserves room-temperature ductility and low density
